title: Can AI Fix Housing and Healthcare Affordability?

reader_summary.headline: We're about 5 million housing units short of what we actually need in the country.
reader_summary.overview: We're about 5 million housing units short of what we actually need in the country. Our goal is to enable fully autonomous buildings. An entire portfolio has the ability to run core operations without requiring human intervention at all.

key_points.text: Housing and healthcare are the biggest expenses that people have.
key_points.evidence_quote: Housing and healthcare are the biggest expenses that people have.

key_points.text: It's pretty self-evident that technology makes the experience better for everyone and brings down costs, and more people should be working on it.

key_points.text: The Lisei is taking on two of the biggest and most expensive challenges we face, housing and healthcare.

key_points.text: Joining me today are my colleague Alex Zimmerman from our growth team, along with the Lisei's co-founders Minna Song and Tony Stoyanov.

thesis: The podcast argues that the housing and healthcare sectors are critical because they consume 42% of household income and 40% of GDP, yet they suffer from massive inefficiencies and a lack of technological adoption compared to other industries. The speakers contend that AI can fix these affordability issues by enabling fully autonomous buildings to reduce operational burdens, increasing housing supply through faster occupancy of vacant units, and creating higher returns for investors to attract more capital.
